inputs.name: validateDocument.input
inputs.description: The candidate game document, of any type, that validateDocument checks; any value that is not a non-null, non-array object with version 1, a non-empty views list and a mechanics list makes the function return only ['Invalid game document']. Ids, titles, condition fields, action targets, and mechanic inputs and events must be 1 to 200 characters and cannot be __proto__, constructor or prototype; descriptions, styles, and scalar string values are capped at 4000 characters; x and y must be finite numbers; and every list holds at most 200 entries.

inputs.name: assertDocument.input
inputs.description: The candidate game document, of any type, that assertDocument checks by calling validateDocument and throwing when that returns any message. A call that returns normally narrows this value to GameDocument, which requires it to clear every check validateDocument runs, under these limits: ids, titles, condition fields, action targets, and mechanic inputs and events are 1 to 200 characters and cannot be __proto__, constructor or prototype; descriptions, styles, and scalar string values are at most 4000 characters; x and y are finite numbers; and every list holds at most 200 entries.

inputs.unknownReason: The assertion establishes the game document type at runtime for callers with unvalidated data.

outputs.name: validateDocument
outputs.description: The list of validation messages for the document, in the order the checks run, and empty only when every check passes. It is exactly ['Invalid game document'] when the top-level shape fails, exactly ['Invalid game view'] when a views entry is not a non-null, non-array object, and otherwise holds one message per failure, such as 'Unknown view: <target>'.

outputs.name: assertDocument
outputs.description: No value is returned: the function has no return statement, so at runtime the result is undefined. Its declared effect is the assertion that input is a GameDocument, which applies only when the call returns without throwing.

errors.name: InvalidGameDocumentError
errors.description: a InvalidGameDocumentError thrown by assertDocument only when validateDocument returns at least one message; its message is those messages joined with '; ' in the order they were produced.
